Let \(x\) be the mass of NaHCO\(_3\) and \(15.00-x\) be the mass of MgCO\(_3\).

Molar masses:
- NaHCO\(_3\) = 84.006 g/mol
- Na\(_2\)CO\(_3\) = 105.988 g/mol
- MgCO\(_3\) = 84.313 g/mol
- MgO = 40.304 g/mol

Residue from NaHCO\(_3\):
\[
2\text{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3
\]
\[
\frac{105.988}{2(84.006)} = 0.630836
\]

Residue from MgCO\(_3\):
\[
\frac{40.304}{84.313} = 0.478028
\]

Mass balance:
\[
0.630836x + 0.478028(15.00-x) = 8.80
\]
\[
0.152808x = 1.62958
\]
\[
x = 10.664 \text{ g}
\]

Mass percentage of NaHCO\(_3\):
\[
\frac{10.664}{15.00} \times 100 = 71.1\%
\]

ANSWER: 71.1
